about: A desktop tool that lines up subtitles with the video they belong to.

prs.title: Batch mode pairs each episode with its own subtitle
prs.broken: When one subtitle was missing in a folder of episodes, each later episode was matched with the next episode's subtitle, then synced and saved.
prs.changed: Episode numbers in file names are no longer mistaken for language tags when pairing files.
prs.matters: A whole season no longer ends up with every subtitle on the wrong episode.

prs.title: Short WebVTT subtitles are no longer lost
prs.broken: Subtitle times without hours, which Whisper writes for videos under an hour, were skipped: shifting left them unmoved and converting to SRT gave an empty file.
prs.changed: These short times are now read, shifted and converted like full ones.
prs.matters: Subtitles made by Whisper sync and convert correctly.

prs.title: ASS to SRT keeps italics and drops comments
prs.broken: Converting ASS subtitles to SRT left style codes in the text, so italics showed as raw markup, and comment lines showed up on screen as part of the previous subtitle.
prs.changed: Italic, bold and underline codes now become SRT tags, other style codes are dropped, and comment lines are skipped.
prs.matters: Converted subtitles look right in any player.

prs.title: TTML subtitles with tick or millisecond times sync again
prs.broken: DFXP and TTML subtitles that give times in ticks or milliseconds were read wrong, so the converted SRT was broken and syncing failed.
prs.changed: Times in ticks, using the file's tick rate, and in milliseconds are now read correctly.
prs.matters: Subtitles from streaming services can be synced.

prs.title: Shifting a DFXP file keeps valid times
prs.broken: Shifting the timing of a DFXP subtitle file by hand wrote times the format does not allow, so players could not read the result.
prs.changed: Shifted times are written as proper clock times.
